summary: Full experiments: the confirmatory runs registered in experiments v04-v17 on T4, A100 and H100 (the v03 proof of concept is the sibling product) (experiments v03-v16). Exactness: the generated kernel holds the same spins as the sequential reference chain on all 13 systems (E1), also in the bitwise and independent bitwise Ising modes (0 of 972 runs differ: 324 each for the shared mode, the independent mode and its 10-round default). Colourings: admissible on every crystal, at the clique bound except sc shells 1-4 (E3). Colouring control (E2, Barker, new seeds): coloured kernel matches exact enumeration (total-variation distance 0.0005-0.0012), all-sites update rejected (0.09-0.51). Physics (E4): 8 critical temperatures within 0.008-0.045%; the triangular-AFM K-point check meets its criterion with per-temperature sampling (v07). Throughput (E6): cost per update does not grow with the batch on the A100 and H100; the independent bitwise Ising mode leads the specialists ising-gpu and cuIsing 2025 at 4096^2 on the H100 and A100 (1.02-1.08x at 10 rounds) but reaches 0.55-0.71x of them at their best size with the default 10 Philox rounds (H5(b) not supported); against the general-purpose GPU codes it is faster at each one's fastest size and equal precision: VAMPIRE at least 26x, BORIS 2.9-5.3x, CUDA-METRO 22-45x (v14, v17). Width law (E5): XLA's unroll factor follows (11) on every grid; u = 4 grids are faster through vector loads, with a magnitude that depends on fusion choices (partially supported). Generality (E9): the nanodisk with exchange shells 1, 2, 4 (7 colours) is computed exactly by changing data only. Against XLA (v15, v16): faster on 66 of 68 held-out grids and at every replica count at fixed geometry, with a cost that varies by up to 1.1x across neighbouring grids against XLA's 1.9x and, for Heisenberg, no upward step when replicas are added.

hypotheses.observed: H100, multi-histogram reweighting, meas 400000, Holm over 8 systems: every reference inside its interval, half widths 0.008-0.045% of Tc (target 0.5%). E4tri (triangular Heisenberg AFM, K-point structure factor, 24/48/96): grows below the crossover as expected, but at T = 0.32 it still grows from 48 to 96 (+0.364 [+0.339, +0.391]); flat only from 96 to 192 (exploratory). v06 triangular-AFM extension (L = 96/192/384, new seeds): growth below the crossover as expected; above it the 192->384 pair still grows slightly (T = 0.32 +0.106 [+0.046, +0.165], T = 0.4 +0.113 [+0.005, +0.215]); the run thinned every temperature by the slowest tau, leaving about 10 samples per chain. v07 (per-temperature sampling, new seeds, ~9 000 samples per chain; run on an NVIDIA H200 that the cloud provider assigned to an H100 request): every pair grows below the crossover; at T = 0.32 the 192->384 log ratio is +0.030 [-0.033, +0.095] and at T = 0.4 -0.003 [-0.011, +0.006], so the K-point side check meets its registered criterion; T = 0.30 still grows (crossover between 0.30 and 0.32 at these sizes). The reference column of E4 held rounded constants for two systems (Ising bcc 6.355, Heisenberg sc 1.4430); against the primary-source values (6.354350 and 1.442929, and the published couplings of the other six) every 95% interval still contains its reference. Registered Barker rerun (experiments v19, registered before it ran; H100, the same sizes, seeds and 400000 measured sweeps): the reference lies inside the Holm-adjusted interval for the square (p Holm 1.00), triangular (1.00), simple cubic (0.38) and face-centred cubic (1.00) Ising lattices, half-widths 0.015-0.066%; the body-centred cubic estimate 6.35493 [6.35457, 6.35532] misses the reference 6.35435 by 0.009% (p Holm 0.015), so the rerun meets its criterion on 4 of 5 lattices (table e4-barker-critical-points-h100.csv). Seed jackknife (post-hoc re-analysis of the saved series, same estimator, Student t on nine degrees of freedom): intervals widen by about 1.2x; the Barker bcc interval [6.35447, 6.35539] still excludes 6.35435 while every other Barker reference and the Metropolis bcc one stay inside, so the bcc miss is an offset of the estimate, not an artefact of the ten-seed interval (table e4-jackknife-critical-points-h100.csv).

hypotheses.statement: Proposal r09. (a) Mechanism: above the device threshold of (11) the XLA unroll factor is gcd(#,4), and no grid below it logs a factor above 1. (b) Cost: on the Heisenberg baseline the paired log-ratio of u = 4 grids against their u = 1 neighbours excludes zero with magnitude at least log 1.3; the sign is reported per device.
hypotheses.metric: unroll factors logged by XLA per grid; paired log cost ratio u = 4 against odd neighbours
hypotheses.test: exact agreement per grid (a); paired bootstrap over 10 interleaved rounds (b)
hypotheses.criterion: (a) factor (11) logged above tC and only factor 1 below, on every grid; (b) per device, pooled Heisenberg log ratio interval excludes zero with |estimate| >= log 1.3 (experiments v04/v05)
hypotheses.observed: Confirmatory runs (experiments v04/v05, new grids, JAX 0.4.35 on every device, interleaved timing with clocks): (a) holds on 12/12 grids on each of T4, A100 and H100. (b) pooled log ratio of u = 4 against odd neighbours: T4 -0.317 [-0.322, -0.311], A100 -0.287 [-0.288, -0.286], H100 -0.249 [-0.249, -0.248]; u = 4 is faster on every device and grid; the log 1.3 magnitude holds on T4 and A100 and misses on H100 by 0.013; no device inconclusive. The v03 T4 reading (u = 4 about 2x slower) does not reproduce. Mechanism (Nsight Compute, H100, diagnostic): u = 4 grids load with ld.global.v4 (16 sectors per request) where u = 1 grids load scalars; log time = 0.49 log DRAM + 0.34 log instructions (R^2 0.96); at L1 = 76/84 the gain is fewer instructions and requests for the same bytes, at L1 = 80 XLA also changes the fusion graph and cuts DRAM traffic by a third, which explains the grid-to-grid spread of the magnitude. v06 per-kernel test (Nsight, new grids L1 = 88/92/96): kernels with vector loads are 30-33% (H100) and 24-26% (A100) faster than in the odd neighbours in every triplet; the criterion holds on the H100 and fails on the A100 at L1 = 92, where untreated kernels fell further. v15, generated kernel against the XLA baseline on 34 held-out grids per device (the XLA vector width is the constant kDefaultUnrollFactor = 4 of its loop emitter; its user cap xla_gpu_max_kernel_unroll_factor is removed and the remaining flag applies to Blackwell only, so neither width nor fusion is controllable from JAX on these GPUs): the generated kernel is faster on 34/34 grids on the A100-80GB (1.48-26.8x) and on 32/34 on the H100; it is slower on the Ising L1 = 108 sweep (0.91x, XLA's vectorized best case; the generated kernel holds 0.030-0.031 ns across L1 = 106-109 while XLA moves 0.028-0.036 ns) and on the Heisenberg 31^3 cube (0.94x, a prime periodic side that forces 31 linear colours). Across each L1 sweep the median cost of XLA varies by up to 1.9x, that of the generated kernel by up to 1.1x. v16, same geometry (sc 27^3) with B = 1..64: the generated kernel is faster at every B on both devices (2.2-27x on the H100, 3.1-27x on the A100); on Heisenberg its cost per update falls monotonically with no upward step on either device, while XLA rises by 20% (H100) and 34% (A100) from B = 32 to 33 and by 44% and 22% from B = 56 to 63; on Ising XLA has two small rises (up to 7.6%) on the H100 and none on the A100, and the generated kernel rises once (B = 32 to 33, 1.67-1.74x) because the packed 32-replica path applies at B = 32 only (on the H100 its B = 33 cost is still below its B = 31 cost; on the A100 it is 11% above). Post-hoc check after experiments v17 (not a registered experiment; requested by the final reviewer): the v15 grids moved to their even neighbours so both sides run periodic (generated kernel at most four colours); the generated kernel is faster on 26/26 grids on the H100 (1.48-16.98x) and on 26/26 on the A100-80GB (1.89-25.85x), and its median cost spread over the slab sweeps is 1.09-1.13 against 1.34-1.68 for XLA (tables e5pp-gen-vs-xla.csv, e5pp-spread.csv).

hypotheses.rationale: Registered criteria, confirmatory data: the mechanism (a) holds on all 36 grids of three devices; the cost (b) holds on T4 and A100 and narrowly misses on H100. The direction is the same everywhere (u = 4 faster), as proposal r11 section 6 now states. The magnitude shortfall on the H100 follows from grid-dependent fusion decisions that (11) does not model, measured with Nsight Compute. Reframed by v15 and v16: XLA's width and fusion are shape heuristics the user cannot control, which makes its cost depend on the grid and on the number of replicas; the generated kernel removes most of that dependence and is faster on 66 of 68 held-out grids and at every replica count. The v15 criterion (faster on every grid) holds on the A100 and not on the H100; the v16 criterion holds for Heisenberg on both devices and fails for Ising on both, because of the generated kernel's own packed path at B = 32.

hypotheses.criterion: (a) slope bound below log 1.05 on the A100 and H100 (v05); (b) at the faster specialist's fastest size, lower 95% bound of the paired log ratio above -log 1.05, per device (r14, v11)
hypotheses.observed: (a) Registered batch-slope test (v05): all 13 systems below the log 1.05 margin on the A100 and the H100. (b) Registered speed test against the specialists (r14, v11; verdict at the v12 default of 10 Philox rounds), independent bitwise Ising mode, at the faster specialist's fastest size: 0.55x on the H100 (-0.606 [-0.612, -0.601], cuIsing 2025 at 32768^2), 0.60x on the A100-80GB (-0.509 [-0.562, -0.468], cuIsing 2025 at 32768^2), 0.71x on the T4 (-0.347 [-0.430, -0.271], cuIsing 2025 at 8192^2, v12 rerun with warm-up and clocks). Ablation at 7 rounds: 0.65x (H100), 0.71x (A100-80GB), 0.94x (T4 v12 rerun); ours leads at 4096^2 on the H100 and the A100 only (1.27x and 1.19x at 7 rounds, 1.08x and 1.02x at 10 rounds) and trails on the T4 at every size; it plateaus near 900/ns on the H100 while ising-gpu and cuIsing 2025 reach 1381-1395/ns at 32768^2; 10 Philox rounds cost about 15%. Heisenberg against VAMPIRE's CUDA Monte Carlo (v12 scan 32^3-64^3 with 4 runs on the H100 and A100; v13 H100 scan 64^3-96^3 with 10 runs; warm-up discarded): VAMPIRE's mean rate on the H100 stays within 0.33-0.44/ns from 48^3 to 96^3, but it varies by about 20% between jobs (sc 64^3: 0.440 in v12, 0.354 in v13) and its per-run rates are bimodal within a job (sc 96^3: 0.295 to 0.442). The equal-precision batch-1 ratio at VAMPIRE's fastest size is therefore job-sensitive: 41-72x (H100, v13), 48-81x (H100, v12), 48-72x against VAMPIRE's single best run on the H100, 56-84x with v12 and v13 pooled at 64^3, and 26-45x on the A100 (v12, 26-57x against its best single run), where the fcc fastest size is the lower edge 32^3. The smallest equal-precision ratio in any definition is 26x; in single precision the ratios are 1.1-2.2x higher. v14, the most recent general GPU Monte Carlo codes, same paired design: BORIS (commit 048503d2; GPU atomistic Monte Carlo exists for sc only; a Linux size_t atomic overload added above sm_80) on the sc Heisenberg ferromagnet, 32^3 to 192^3: BORIS plateaus at 7.7-8.0/ns from 128^3 on the H100 and 3.3-3.5/ns from 80^3 on the A100; at its fastest size the generated kernel is 2.9x (single, [2.5, 3.3]) and 5.3x (double) faster on the H100 and 4.6x and 5.3x on the A100, and faster at every size (2.5-6.4x). CUDA-METRO (commit cbc9737f, JOSS; approximate synchronous P-site update; its site index int(L^2 u) with u in (0, 1] is clamped to L^2 - 1 before timing) on the 2D triangular Heisenberg ferromagnet, L = 256-4096, at its fastest P: 2.0-40x (float32, equal precision) and 1.24-30x (float64) on both devices, the smallest ratios at L = 4096 where the generated kernel's rate falls from 12/ns (L = 1024) to 0.57/ns (H100) as the lattice outgrows the L2 cache; against CUDA-METRO's own usable-P ceiling 2.5-96x. v17, after Nsight Compute showed register spills in one-row programs longer than 1024 sites (0, 18 M and 253 M local-memory sectors at rows of 1024, 2048 and 4096 sites), long rows are chunked: the generated kernel holds 11.7-12.6/ns (H100) and 6.3-6.9/ns (A100) from L = 1024 to 4096 instead of falling to 0.57/ns, and the CUDA-METRO ratio at its fastest P becomes 36-45x (float32) and 7.0-9.6x (float64) at L = 1024-4096 on both devices. Post-hoc memory profile after experiments v17 (Nsight Compute, H100, one sweep, state above the 50 MB L2): vector-spin passes move 2.03 TB/s (Heisenberg sc 64^3, 60.5% of the 3.35 TB/s peak) and 2.47-2.54 TB/s (Heisenberg fcc 32^3, 73.7-75.9%); the multi-spin-coded Ising mode moves 0.29 TB/s (8.7%) at 72.4% SM throughput, so it is instruction-bound (table e5-roofline-h100.csv).

novelty.claim: A single exact Metropolis kernel, generated from lattice data through linear colourings, serves Ising, XY and Heisenberg models on crystals with a basis and longer-range exchange without per-system code; it is faster than the general-purpose GPU Monte Carlo codes VAMPIRE, BORIS and CUDA-METRO and than an XLA array program, and its cost does not depend on compiler decisions about the grid shape or the number of replicas.
novelty.rationale: Exactness holds spin by spin on 13 systems and 9 crystals on three GPUs, the physics recovers 8 critical temperatures, and the nanodisk with exchange shells 1, 2 and 4 is computed by changing data only. At equal precision and at each competitor's fastest size the generated kernel is faster than VAMPIRE (at least 26x), BORIS (2.9-5.3x) and CUDA-METRO (22-45x in float32, 7-30x in float64, with the v17 long-row correction; exact where CUDA-METRO is approximate), and faster than the XLA baseline on 66 of 68 held-out grids and at every replica count, with a cost that varies by up to 1.1x across neighbouring grids against XLA's 1.9x. It is not faster than the 2D-Ising specialists ising-gpu and cuIsing 2025 at their best size (0.55-0.71x), which serve one model on one lattice.

qualitative.title: Energy histograms against the exact distribution
qualitative.method: sampled energy histograms of the coloured kernel and of the all-sites update overlaid on exact enumeration, Metropolis and Barker acceptance
qualitative.reading: Under Metropolis the coloured kernel over-weights high-energy levels on the 3x3 triangular lattice (E = 1 and E = 9); under Barker it overlays the exact distribution, while the all-sites update stays far off in both.

limitations: E4 deviated from the declared measurement length (20000 to 400000 sweeps) after a first inconclusive run; the tau probe hit its cap at three sizes.
Kaggle jobs were pushed with the Kaggle CLI and Modal runs with modal run, not through remote_cli, so there is no remote-execution ledger.
H1b, H4 and H5 rest on runs registered before they were made (experiments v04/v05); their earlier forms were restated after the v03 data.

Against ising-gpu and cuIsing 2025 at their best lattice size the independent bitwise mode is 0.55x (H100), 0.60x (A100-80GB) and 0.71x (T4) with the default 10 Philox rounds (0.65x, 0.71x and 0.94x at the 7-round ablation); its lead holds only at 4096^2 on the H100 and the A100 (1.08x and 1.02x at 10 rounds); on the T4 it trails at every size.

VAMPIRE runs in double precision with a host copy per step; the batch-1 equal-precision ratios at VAMPIRE's fastest size are the fair comparison, the batch-128 ratios measure batching as well. VAMPIRE's own rate varies by about 20% between jobs, so the ratio is reported as a job-sensitive range (26-84x across jobs and definitions, at least 26x); the A100 was not rescanned beyond 64^3 and its fcc fastest size is the lower edge of the scan.
E8 (two GPUs) is supplementary: the claims concern one device.

The H5(b) verdict rounds changed after data were seen: v11 registered the bitwise mode with 7 Philox rounds; after the v11 run the default became 10 rounds (proposal r15, experiments v12) and the verdict moved with it. The change is conservative: at 10 rounds every ratio is lower (0.55-0.71x against 0.65-0.94x), and the 7-round values remain reported as an ablation.

With linear colourings a periodic box whose side is prime needs as many colours as the side (31 colours at 31^3), which multiplies the launches; sides with small factors avoid it, and merging colour classes that share no bond is left as future work.

Rows longer than 1024 sites spilled registers in a one-row float program (Nsight Compute, H100); they are now chunked over grid axis 2 (v17), which restored 11.7-12.6/ns at L = 1024-4096. The v14 CUDA-METRO ratios at L = 2048-4096 (1.24-6.5x) were measured before this correction and are kept as recorded; a sc row of 1152 sites runs about 20% slower chunked (one full and one short chunk).

BORIS offers GPU atomistic Monte Carlo on the simple cubic mesh only and uses a cone move adapting toward 50% acceptance; CUDA-METRO's square and honeycomb kernels are defective at the pinned commit, so it is paired on the triangular lattice only, and its out-of-range site index was clamped before timing.

The v15 XLA criterion holds on the A100 and not on the H100 (two of 34 grids), and the v16 smoothness criterion fails for Ising on both devices because the generated kernel's packed path applies at B = 32 only.

contribution_type.why: A method paper backed by wide validation. H1: 0 differing spins on 13 systems, plus 0/108 per device in both bitwise modes. H1b: Barker, 0/10 seeds rejected. H2: admissible colourings. H3: 8 Tc within 0.008-0.045%, K-point met at v07. H5: flat batch cost on the A100 and H100, while against the specialists at their best size the bitwise mode reaches 0.55-0.71x with the default 10 Philox rounds (H5(b) not supported). Novelty is 'justified'. H4 is 'partially_supported' and the stage is still 'poc', but no central verdict is not_supported.

General.why: Generator, exactness, colourings, critical temperatures and paired throughput on three GPUs; H1, H1b, H2 and H3 are supported, H5 is partially supported (H5(b), the speed test against the specialists, is not).

Use-Inspired.why: The E9 nanodisk with shells 1, 2, 4 (7 colours, data-only change) has a table and a figure, but it is one demonstration (2799/2800 points within precision), not a physics result checked against a reference.

Concept & Feasibility.why: discussion.json says stage 'poc', but support is well beyond pilot scale (H3 and H5 on H100/A100); the general float kernel is still 7.2x (H100) to 10.3x (T4) slower than ising-gpu.

Theory.why: Eqs. (7)-(8) and (11) are mathematical but are checked by experiment (H2, H4), not proved; optimality stays open for sc shells 1-4.

Negative Results.why: No central hypothesis is not_supported; the H4 magnitude miss (0.013 on the H100) and the Metropolis bias are side results.
